title: Caffeine three times a day, the last dose 8 hours before bed: what the sleep lab recorded [dose, recording]
teaser: Twenty young men who drink caffeine every day took 150 mg three times a day, the last dose 8 hours before bed. [sample, dose, recording] Their measured sleep did not differ from their placebo nights. [sleep_same] One thing in the brain recordings did. [sigma]
hook: The usual advice is to stop caffeine by noon. [-] A sleep laboratory tested something closer to how people actually take it: morning, midday and mid-afternoon, every day. [schedule]
populationPanel: Who was studied: twenty healthy men aged 18 to 35 who already had 300 to 600 mg of caffeine a day and slept well. [sample, who, good_sleepers] Each man went through all three conditions in random order without knowing which capsules he was taking. [blind] The result describes men like these. [lim_male] It says nothing yet about women, older adults or people who rarely have caffeine. [lim_male, lim_young, not_after_abstinence]

sections.heading: What they did
paragraphs: For 10 days at a time the men swallowed a capsule three times a day: 45, 255 and 475 minutes after waking. [schedule] In one condition every capsule held 150 mg of caffeine. [dose] In another, all were placebo. [dose] In a third, caffeine was swapped for placebo near the end, to see what stopping does. [dose]
After 9 days they slept in the laboratory wired to an EEG, with bedtime falling 8 hours after the last caffeine capsule. [recording]

sections.heading: What they found
paragraphs: Total sleep time, the time taken to fall asleep and the share of each sleep stage did not differ between the caffeine nights and the placebo nights. [sleep_same] The men's own ratings of how they slept did not differ either. [quality_same] The researchers had expected to see less deep sleep on caffeine and did not find it. [no_depth_change]

sections.heading: How sure is that?
paragraphs: Here the paper gives less than we would like. [-] Its text reports these comparisons only as not statistically significant, with p above 0.05, and gives no effect size and no confidence interval. [sleep_same] With twenty people, a real difference of a few minutes could sit inside that result unnoticed. [sample, lim_n] Read it as: no large disruption was detected in this group. [sleep_same] It is not proof that there is none. [-]

sections.heading: What most summaries miss
paragraphs: One measure did change. [-] During non-REM sleep, brain activity in the sigma band was lower on caffeine nights than on placebo nights. [sigma] The authors read this as an early sign of withdrawal, already present 8 hours after the last dose. [sigma_meaning] In other words, a daily habit may mean beginning a small withdrawal every night and undoing it with the first cup every morning. [daily_reverse]
A second detail comes from the nights at home: on caffeine, the men went to bed about 25 minutes later than on placebo. [later_bed]

sections.heading: A related idea
paragraphs: Tolerance ties this together. [-] The authors cite earlier work in which a week of regular caffeine blunted its effect on sleep, even at high evening doses. [tolerance] They also warn that the same morning cup could still disturb sleep in someone coming off several days without any. [not_after_abstinence] The habit, not just the cup, shapes the night. [-]

limitations: Only men took part, so the result may not hold for women. [lim_male]
All were aged 18 to 35. [who] The authors note that middle-aged people are more vulnerable to what caffeine does to sleep. [lim_young]
Twenty participants is a small trial, and the text gives no effect sizes to show how small a difference it could have missed. [sample, lim_n]

takeaways: The schedule tested was three doses, the last one 475 minutes after waking, which came 8 hours before bed. [schedule, recording]
The finding covers a steady daily habit. [who] The authors caution that it may not hold after several days without caffeine. [not_after_abstinence]
Bedtime at home drifted about 25 minutes later on caffeine, so watch the clock as well as the cup. [later_bed]

steps.label: Last caffeine at least 8 hours before bed
steps.detail: The gap this trial tested. It did not test anything shorter.

steps.label: In bed within 30 minutes of my usual time
steps.detail: Participants were asked to keep to this at home. The trial did not test it, so it carries no weight.

words.alt: A falling curve shows how much of a dose of caffeine is left in the hours after you take it. [caffeine-saliva-half-life/half_life_caffeine] A shaded band around the curve shows how much people in that study differed. [caffeine-saliva-half-life/half_life_caffeine]
words.halfLifeNote: That half-life comes from another study: twelve young volunteers took 25 mg of caffeine on its own, measured in their saliva. [caffeine-saliva-half-life/crossover_design, caffeine-saliva-half-life/arm_a_dose, caffeine-saliva-half-life/matrix_saliva]
